skill.description: Reviews influencer content submissions against campaign briefs, brand guidelines, FTC disclosure needs, and platform requirements. Produces approve, revise, or reject decisions with creator feedback.
skill.summary: Reviews influencer submissions for brand fit, claim accuracy, disclosure compliance, and creator feedback.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static filesystem and command-execution alerts are Markdown links, code spans, or workflow labels rather than executable behavior. One risk remains: the standalone fallback trusts mutable raw GitHub files from the main branch. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle required reference files with the skill, or pin the raw GitHub fallback to an immutable commit and require user confirmation before network fetches.

content.value_statement: Influencer submissions can miss brand rules, required claims, or disclosure requirements before launch. This skill applies a structured review and gives a clear decision with creator-ready feedback.
actual_capabilities: Checks submissions against campaign briefs, brand guidelines, and required messages.
Reviews FTC disclosure, platform rules, claim substantiation, and required campaign elements.
Scores brand alignment, message accuracy, compliance, creative quality, and technical fit.
Issues one gate decision: approved, minor changes, revisions required, or rejected.
Creates constructive feedback that a campaign team can send to the creator.
Records structured handoff fields for follow-up campaign workflows.
limitations: It needs the content, campaign brief, platform, and disclosure context to make a reliable decision.
It does not draft the original influencer brief or partnership contract.
It is not legal advice and cannot replace review by counsel for regulated claims.
It may need current platform rules or local reference files for detailed technical checks.

use_cases.title: Approve Creator Drafts
use_cases.description: Review a creator post before launch and decide whether it is ready, needs changes, or must be rejected.

use_cases.title: Check Sponsored Disclosure
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether sponsored content includes clear disclosure and avoids unsupported product claims.

use_cases.title: Prepare Creator Feedback
use_cases.description: Turn review notes into a direct, constructive message that explains required edits.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Submission Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with pasted content and a short brief.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this influencer content submission for approval. Use the brief, platform, and disclosure context below, then give one decision and creator feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Brand and Message Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review focused on brand fit and campaign message accuracy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this creator draft against our brand guidelines and required messages. Identify missing claims, prohibited claims, brand safety issues, and required changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compliance Gate Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for sponsored or regulated content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a compliance review for this sponsored post. Check disclosure placement, platform requirements, claim substantiation, required elements, and rejection triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Full Launch Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced end-to-end review before publication or amplification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this influencer submission for launch readiness. Score each category, explain evidence, apply veto rules, map the status, and draft final creator feedback.

output_examples.input: A TikTok draft for a protein powder campaign has strong visuals but no sponsored disclosure.
output_examples.output: Decision: Rejected. The content needs a clear sponsored disclosure before resubmission. The feedback also asks the creator to add the required promo code and protein message.

output_examples.input: An Instagram Reel includes the correct disclosure but misses one required campaign hashtag.
output_examples.output: Decision: Approved with minor changes. The review confirms brand fit and compliance, then asks for the missing hashtag before posting.

output_examples.input: A YouTube Short uses an unsupported health claim and omits the required product disclaimer.
output_examples.output: Decision: Revisions required or rejected based on claim risk. The output separates must-fix compliance items from optional creative improvements.

best_practices: Provide the brief, creator handle, platform, content type, required messages, and disclosure context.
Attach or paste brand guidelines and any prohibited claim list before asking for a decision.
Use the feedback message as a starting point and adjust tone for the creator relationship.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a final decision without giving the campaign criteria or platform context.
Do not treat this skill as legal approval for regulated industries or high-risk claims.
Do not publish rejected content after only fixing cosmetic issues when disclosure or claim integrity failed.

faq.question: What kind of content can it review?
faq.answer: It can review captions, post descriptions, video notes, image notes, and linked submissions when enough context is provided.

faq.question: Does it decide if content is approved?
faq.answer: Yes. It produces one gate decision and explains the evidence behind that decision.

faq.question: Can it review FTC disclosure?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks disclosure presence, clarity, placement, and sponsored content context. It is not legal advice.

faq.question: Does it create the campaign brief?
faq.answer: No. It reviews submissions after a brief exists. Use a brief generation workflow before this skill.

faq.question: Can it write feedback for creators?
faq.answer: Yes. It produces constructive feedback that explains what works, what must change, and why.

faq.question: What inputs improve accuracy?
faq.answer: Give the campaign goal, platform, disclosure status, brand rules, required messages, prohibited claims, and technical specs.
